record.final_answer:
分别针对两篇论文的问题，按声明顺序回答如下。

**第一篇：《A BERT-Based Transfer Learning Approach for Hate Speech Detection in Online Social Media》（1910.12574）——作者提供了哪些证据表明模型能捕捉数据标注与收集中的偏差？**

作者在摘要中总结道，模型可以 "capture some biases in data annotation and collection process" [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s10:p0:c0-1410]。具体证据来自错误分析：
1. **数据收集偏差**：Waseem 等人使用小规模临时关键词集合，Davidson 等人使用众包关键词词典（Hatebase 词典）来抽样推文，导致收集数据中包含偏差。尤其是 Davidson 数据集过度抽样了用非裔美国人白话英语（AAVE）书写、地理上限于美国的推文，其中包含 "nigga"、"faggot"、"coon"、"queer" 等贬损词，造成较高的误分类率 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s8:p2:c0-2000]。
2. **数据标注偏差**：标注者在毫无社交背景（如说话者身份、方言）预设的情况下，把许多含不敬词汇的样本标注为仇恨或冒犯性内容，而这些推文其实只是冒犯性甚至两者皆非；模型在这些样本上的“错误”实际暴露了标注规则的偏差，而非分类器本身性能低 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s8:p2:c0-2000]。
3. 摘要与结论进一步指出，检查结果表明模型具备检测数据收集或标注过程中偏差的能力，可为未来利用预训练 BERT 去除仇恨言论数据集偏差提供线索 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s9:p0:c0-1312] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s0:p6:c0-512]。作者还解释，这得益于 BERT 在普通语料上预训练所获得的一般性知识，使其在数据有偏差的情况下仍能准确区分仇恨与冒犯样本 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s8:p2:c0-2000]。

**第二篇：《Follow Alice into the Rabbit Hole: Giving Dialogue Agents Understanding of Human Level Attributes》（1910.08293）——数据集如何建模角色档案？**

该数据集通过将详细的**人类级属性（HLAs）**与特定角色的对话数据相结合来建模角色档案 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.08293:s32:p0:c0-1367]：
- HLA 是代表虚构角色档案与身份的特征，基于从 TV Tropes 收集的“套路（tropes）”——即反复出现、由观众印象决定的虚构人物性格特征 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.08293:s33:p0:c1709-3703]；
- 基于“档案与身份有效影响语言风格”的假设，数据集让对话代理能够通过 HLA 学习角色的语言风格，且对话数据可回溯到其语境及相应的人性化属性 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.08293:s0:p2:c0-1135] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.08293:s32:p0:c0-1367]。

以上为两篇论文各自独立问题的回答，二者问题相互独立，不作共同排序或比较排名。

record.final_answer: Multi-agent dual learning (MADL) extends the dual learning framework—where the primal task (X→Y) and dual task (Y→X) boost each other—by introducing multiple primal and dual models [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s34:p0:c0-1887]. Concretely, it uses N primal translation models f_i (X→Y) and N dual translation models g_j (Y→X), all pre-trained on bilingual data, and eventually outputs one f_0 and one g_0 for inference [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277]. Each model has a non-negative hyperparameter weight, and the models are combined into F_α (X→Y) and G_β (Y→X) with weights summing to 1; for any input, F_α and G_β produce outputs by maximizing the weighted sum of the log-probabilities from the member models [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277]. Training minimizes the standard likelihood of f_0 and g_0 on bilingual data, plus terms on monolingual data that encourage round-trip reconstruction—P(x|G_β(F_α(x))) for X-side data and P(y|F_α(G_β(y))) for Y-side data—so translation quality improves in both directions [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277].

该论文的系统在 WMT19 共享新闻翻译任务的 11 个语言方向上评测：德语↔英语、德语↔法语、中文↔英语、英语→立陶宛语、英语→芬兰语、俄语→英语这 6 组（8 个方向）获得第一名，另外 3 个方向——立陶宛语→英语、芬兰语→英语、英语→哈萨克语——获得第二名 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s0:p0:c0-501]。

**论文二：An Analysis of Word2Vec for the Italian Language（2001.09332）—— 词嵌入是否在某个 NLP 任务上测试？**

是的。训练出的意大利语 Word2Vec 词嵌入在词类比（word analogy）这一 NLP 任务上评测：测试集包含 19,791 个类比，分为 19 个类别，涵盖“语义”宏观领域（8,915 个）和“句法”宏观领域（10,876 个），任务形式如“man : woman = king : ?”需猜出目标词 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:2001.09332:s14:p0:c0-1886]。准确率分别用加法余弦距离（3COSADD）和乘法余弦距离（3COSMUL）计算，并与文献中两种已有意大利语嵌入模型对比，该论文模型性能显著更优 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:2001.09332:s17:p0:c0-1998]。

以上按顺序分别回答两个问题，两篇论文之间不做共同排名的推断。

record.final_answer: MADL extends dual learning, which exploits the duality between the primal task (X→Y) and dual task (Y→X) to boost both directions. Instead of one model per direction, MADL uses N pre-trained primal models f_i: X→Y and N dual models g_j: Y→X, each with non-negative hyper-parameter weights α_i and β_j. These are combined into ensemble models F_α (X→Y) and G_β (Y→X) that maximize weighted sums of log-probabilities when translating. Training then optimizes f_0 and g_0 not only on the bilingual data but also on monolingual data via reconstruction through the combined models — maximizing log P(x | G_β(F_α(x))) for x-monolingual data and log P(y | F_α(G_β(y))) for y-monolingual data [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s5:p0:c0-786][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277]. At inference only f_0 and g_0 are used [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s5:p0:c0-786].

record.final_answer: MADL is an enhanced version of dual learning that uses N primal translation models fᵢ (X→Y) and N dual translation models gⱼ (Y→X), all pre-trained on bilingual data, eventually outputting one f₀ and one g₀ for inference. Each primal model fᵢ has a non-negative weight αᵢ and each dual model gⱼ a non-negative weight βⱼ (hyper-parameters summing to 1). These weights combine the models into two ensemble translation models: F_α = Σ αᵢfᵢ and G_β = Σ βⱼgⱼ. For any x ∈ X, F_α(x) picks ŷ = argmax Σ αᵢ log P(ỹ|x; fᵢ), and similarly G_β(y) picks the best x̂ for y ∈ Y. Training optimizes f₀ and g₀ on the bilingual dataset B with the standard likelihood objectives, plus two dual reconstruction (round-trip) terms on monolingual data: minimizing -log P(x | G_β(F_α(x))) over monolingual X data and -log P(y | F_α(G_β(y))) over monolingual Y data, so the primal and dual ensembles reconstruct each other's inputs and boost both translation directions [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s34:p0:c0-1887].

record.final_answer: In Table 2, ALOHA reaches a Hits@1/20 of 0.3642, versus 0.3032 for the strongest baseline (Uniform Model), 0.2642 for Poly-encoder, 0.1918 for BERT bi-ranker, 0.1210 for Kvmemnn, and 0.0597 for Feed Yourself — so ALOHA is about 0.061 Hits@1/20 above the best baseline and roughly 0.10–0.30 above the weaker baselines. ALOHA also improves Hits@5/20 (0.6816 vs 0.6166), Hits@10/20 (0.8520 vs 0.8090), Mean Rank (4.8154 vs 5.5680), MRR (0.5114 vs 0.4542), F1 (0.3901 vs 0.4385 — here the Uniform Model is higher), and BLEU (0.2867 vs 0.2393) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.08293:s42:p0:c0-662]. 绘画嵌入方面，模型使用**3个CNN**提取绘画特征，输入由2个判别器提供对抗反馈的RNN生成器来生成英文诗歌 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c0-2000]。语言风格迁移方面，使用**带全局注意力的seq2seq模型**将诗歌转化为莎士比亚风格散文（并与带指针网络的seq2seq模型对比，全局注意力版本效果更佳）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c0-2000]。

**2）《Knowledge Graph Representation with Jointly Structural and Textual Encoding》(1611.08661)：对比基线**

链接预测任务的基线 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.08661:s18:p0:c0-1435]：

- TransE、TransH、TransR、CTransR、TransD、TranSparse

其Jointly模型（CBOW、LSTM、A-LSTM）在各项指标上均超过TransE，但在FB15K链接预测的Hits@10上TransD表现更好 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.08661:s19:p0:c0-1670]。

record.final_answer: They measure a community's temporal dynamism via language. At the word level, a word's volatility captures how ephemeral/time-specific it is (computed per time period using PMI-style comparisons, analogous to their specificity measure, but across time). Community-level dynamicity is then defined as the average volatility of all utterances in a community: a highly dynamic community constantly shifts interests from one time window to another, reflected in its use of volatile language; a community whose language stays consistent over time is called stable [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c0-2000].

record.final_answer:
以下分别按两篇论文回答（两问题彼此独立，不做跨论文排序）：

**1. 主题如何提取？**
- 论文 1910.04006（精神科再入院风险预测）：主题提取使用作者前期工作（Holderness et al., 2019）提出、并在院内心因科 EHR 文本上预训练的 NLP 流水线。先从 Research Patient Data Registry 的约 800 万句 EHR 句子中生成 Universal Sentence Encoder 式嵌入，再用多层感知机（MLP）分类器自动将句子标注到七个风险因素领域（外表、思维过程、思维内容、人际、物质使用、职业、情绪），主题提取组件达到 0.828 F1 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s4:p2:c0-415]。
- 论文 1705.09665（多社区生态中的社区认同与用户参与）不涉及主题提取：该文研究的是基于语言使用的社区认同刻画，而非主题抽取，语料中未见相关方法描述。

**2. 如何衡量社区的时间动态性？**
- 论文 1705.09665：在词层面，通过 PMI 类比较（与特异度 specificity 类似但沿时间轴计算）刻画词的"波动性/ephemeral"程度；在社区层面，动态性（dynamicity）定义为社区中所有话语的平均波动性——高度动态的社区不断从一个时间窗口转换兴趣，体现为波动性语言的使用；语言随时间保持一致的社区称为"稳定"（stable）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c0-2000]。
- 论文 1910.04006 不涉及该问题：它不做社区动态性测量，其研究主题是 EHR 特征与精神科再入院预测，语料中未见相关内容。

**1. 主题如何提取？**
- 论文 1910.04006（精神科再入院风险预测）：主题提取使用作者前期工作（Holderness et al., 2019）提出、并在院内心因科 EHR 文本上预训练的 NLP 流水线。先从 Research Patient Data Registry 的约 800 万句 EHR 句子中生成 Universal Sentence Encoder 式嵌入，再用多层感知机（MLP）分类器自动将句子标注到七个风险因素领域（外表、思维过程、思维内容、人际、物质使用、职业、情绪），主题提取组件达到 0.828 F1 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s4:p2:c0-415]。
- 论文 1705.09665（多社区生态中的社区认同与用户参与）不涉及主题提取：该文研究的是基于语言使用的社区认同刻画，而非主题抽取，语料中未见相关方法描述。

**2. 如何衡量社区的时间动态性？**
- 论文 1705.09665：在词层面，通过 PMI 类比较（与特异度 specificity 类似但沿时间轴计算）刻画词的"波动性/ephemeral"程度；在社区层面，动态性（dynamicity）定义为社区中所有话语的平均波动性——高度动态的社区不断从一个时间窗口转换兴趣，体现为波动性语言的使用；语言随时间保持一致的社区称为"稳定"（stable）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c0-2000]。

record.final_answer: In the paper 1705.09665, temporal dynamism is captured through word-level volatility, defined via pointwise mutual information: the volatility of a word w at time t in community c is Vct(w) = log Pct(w) / PcT(w) — the PMI of w in time window ct relative to the community's entire history cT. A word is volatile at time t if it occurs more frequently in that window than across the community's history, i.e., a short-lived fad [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c1821-3568]. This is then extended from words to utterances (average volatility of words in the utterance), and community-level dynamicity is defined as the average volatility of all utterances in each time window ct; communities whose language stays consistent over time are called stable [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c1821-3568].

**问题1:《评估临床情感分析与主题抽取在精神科再入院风险预测中的效果》(1910.04006)——他们如何抽取主题?**

该论文沿用其先前工作(Holderness et al., 2019)的主题抽取与情感分析流水线,并在内部精神科EHR文本上预训练:首先用一个由临床医生确定的领域相关关键词和多词表达构成的词库,将EHR句子自动标注到七个风险因素领域(外表、思维过程、思维内容、人际、物质使用、职业、情绪),无需人工标注;然后用通用句子编码器(USE,一个在大规模通用网络数据上预训练的transformer注意力网络)将句子向量化;标注到至少一个领域的句子再通过七个领域对应的临床情感MLP分类器(以两个隐藏层和0.75的dropout防止过拟合,训练于3,500条由三名临床医生标注的EHR句子)处理。主题抽取组件的整体F1为0.828 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c1732-3263]。

**问题2:《多社区格局中的社区身份与用户参与》(1705.09665)——作者如何衡量社区在时间上的动态性?**

该论文通过逐点互信息(PMI)在词级别定义"波动性"(volatility):词w在社区c的时段t的波动性为 Vct(w) = log Pct(w) / PcT(w),即w在该时间窗口的出现频率相对该社区整个历史cT的PMI;若某词在t时段的出现频率高于其整个历史频率,即为波动词(短暂的流行) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c1821-3568]。词级别度量随后扩展到话语(话语取其中各词的平均波动性),社区层面的"动态性"(dynamicity)则定义为该社区每个时间窗口内所有话语的平均波动性;语言随时间相对一致的社区被称为"稳定"的 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396]。

record.final_answer: The authors measure a community's temporal dynamism (dynamicity) with a language-based, word-level volatility measure computed over time windows. Word-level measures are computed for each time period of a community's history using pointwise mutual information (PMI), and these are aggregated to the community level. As they put it: "we define the dynamicity of a community INLINEFORM0 as the average volatility of all utterances in INLINEFORM1" [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c0-2000]. In other words, a highly dynamic community constantly shifts interests from one time window to another, reflected in volatile language, while a stable community's language remains relatively consistent over time [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396]. For example, Seahawks shows very dynamic language as discussion shifts throughout the football season, whereas Cooking and pics remain stable [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c0-2000]. Note that because these measures are averaged across time, the study treats community identity as a static property [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s12:p2:c0-974].

分别回答两个问题（两篇论文不构成任何统一排序）：

一、《Assessing the Efficacy of Clinical Sentiment Analysis and Topic Extraction in Psychiatric Readmission Risk Prediction》（1910.04006）如何提取主题？
该论文使用其先前工作（Holderness et al., 2019）提出的自动主题提取与临床情感分析流水线，该流水线基于院内精神科 EHR 文本预训练。具体做法是：先从 Partners HealthCare 的 Research Patient Data Registry (RPDR) 中抽取的 800 万句（3.4 亿词）EHR 句子上训练一个多层感知机（MLP）分类器，自动识别句子所属的七个风险因子领域（外表、思维过程、思维内容、人际、物质使用、职业、情绪），进而从自由文本叙事中提取主题特征。其主题提取组件的总体性能约为 0.828 F1 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000]。当前可见文本未显示具体的主题模型算法（如 LDA），故无法确认。

二、《Community Identity and User Engagement in a Multi-Community Landscape》（1705.09665）如何衡量社区在时间上的动态性？
作者采用基于语言的词级易变性度量：对社区历史的每个时间段用点互信息（PMI）计算词级指标，再聚合到社区层面——"we define the dynamicity of a community INLINEFORM0 as the average volatility of all utterances in INLINEFORM1"（即社区动态性定义为其中所有话语的平均易变性）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c0-2000]。高度动态的社区在各时间窗口间不断转移兴趣，语言易变；语言随时间保持相对一致的社区则被视为稳定的。例如 Seahawks（足球队）随赛季推进话题不断变化、动态性很高，而 Cooking 和 pics 整体保持稳定 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c0-2000]。需注意这些指标是对时间取平均的，因此该研究将社区身份视为静态属性 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s12:p2:c0-974]。

MCScript (1803.05223) was built through crowdsourcing on Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk), in several steps [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s16:p0:c0-1994][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s1:p0:c0-631]:

1. Pilot studies: The authors first ran three pilot studies to find the best way to collect questions requiring commonsense inference. Showing workers full texts produced questions too lexically close to the text; reusing questions across texts of the same scenario produced mostly nonsensical pairings. In a third pilot, workers were shown no specific text at all but asked to formulate questions about a script scenario (e.g., EATING IN A RESTAURANT), which yielded the right level of specificity [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s16:p0:c0-1994][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s16:p0:c1682-3678].

2. Scenario selection: Based on this, the collection was anchored on 110 script scenarios (80 selected from existing script resources, 20 new, plus 10 from InScript) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s16:p0:c1682-3678].

3. Texts: Following Modi et al. (2016), workers wrote a story about a given activity "as if explaining it to a child," yielding simple, explicit, scenario-centered texts; 20 texts were collected per scenario [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s16:p0:c1682-3678].

4. Questions: Workers, shown no concrete story, were told to imagine testing whether a child understood a story about the scenario, writing 15 questions each (3 temporal, 3 content, 3 reasoning, 6 free), from 10 participants per scenario, using the neutral pronoun "they" for the protagonist [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s16:p0:c3414-5414].

5. Answers and validation: Answers were collected via additional HITs (finding 15 answer pairs per HIT); the full dataset was then manually validated, replacing inappropriate answers (about 11.5% of questions had at least one answer replaced) and excluding 135 questions (~1%) for which no appropriate answer could be found [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s17:p0:c3496-5496].

Overall, more than 2,100 texts were paired with 15 questions each (~32,000 annotated questions), and after filtering (excluding ~13% without worker agreement and validation) the final dataset contains 13,939 questions, of which 3,827 (27.4%) require commonsense/script knowledge [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1803.05223:s17:p0:c3496-5496].

The paper presents four new fine-tuning approaches built on pre-trained BERTbase for hate speech classification [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s15:p0:c1686-3370]:
1. BERT based fine-tuning — uses only the [CLS] token output (from the 12th transformer encoder) fed to a fully connected network without hidden layers, with softmax classification.
2. Insert nonlinear layers — adds a fully connected classifier with two hidden layers (size 768, Leaky ReLU activations, softmax output) on top of BERT.
3. Insert Bi-LSTM layer — feeds all outputs of the latest transformer encoder into a bidirectional LSTM, then classifies via a fully connected softmax layer.
4. Insert CNN layer — concatenates the output vectors of all transformer encoders and applies a convolution plus max pooling before a fully connected softmax classifier.

These are shown in Figure 1 as the four fine-tuning strategies [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s16:p0:c0-1996]. Among them, the CNN-based fine-tuning strategy gave the best F1 results (88% on Waseem, 92% on Davidson) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s7:p2:c0-2000].

record.final_answer: The paper does not train a selector on annotated selections (none exist). Instead, content selection β is treated as a latent variable: the source and target are available, but ground-truth selections are unknown, so the selector and generator are co-trained end-to-end by maximizing a lower bound of the marginal data likelihood, using amortized variational inference (lower training variance than reinforcement-based selection). The decoder is modified so that pθ(Y|X,β) initializes its hidden states from a mean pooling over the selected contents and unselected contents are blocked from attention, so selection decisions are learned from the generation objective alone [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s20:p0:c0-1927] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s0:p3:c0-1017] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s17:p0:c0-901].

record.final_answer: The model treats content selection as latent variables and trains with amortized variational inference, which gives lower training variance than Reinforce-select; the selector and generator are co-trained within the same objective, so generations stay faithful to selected contents [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s19:p0:c0-1996]. The VRS variant uses the REINFORCE algorithm for gradient estimation, with the only extra parameter φ being a simple MLP [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s22:p0:c1614-3608]. Instead of training the selector on heuristic rules, β is treated as a latent variable and selector and generator are co-trained by maximizing the marginal data likelihood, letting the selector automatically explore optimal selecting strategies [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s20:p0:c0-1927]. Additionally, limiting the KL-term is used to control the selecting strategy, and a selecting-ratio constraint is applied in training (per Eq. 4) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s8:p0:c0-1341][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s22:p0:c1614-3608].

Based on the currently visible excerpts of the paper, the topic extraction is done through an NLP pipeline for feature extraction that works as follows:

- Topic extraction and clinical sentiment scores are obtained automatically via a pipeline introduced in the authors' prior work (Holderness et al., 2019), which was pretrained on in-house psychiatric EHR text [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s4:p2:c0-415].

- Specifically, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier is trained on EHR sentences — 8,000,000 sentences consisting of 340,000,000 tokens — extracted from the Research Patient Data Registry (RPDR), a centralized regional clinical data repository of the Partners HealthCare network, and these sentences are automatically identified and labeled for their respective (risk factor) categories [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000].

record.final_answer:
Topic extraction in this paper is not classic LDA-style topic modeling; instead, the authors use an NLP pipeline (from their prior work, Holderness et al. 2019) that assigns EHR admission-note sentences to seven clinically defined risk factor domains (Appearance, Thought Process, Thought Content, Interpersonal, Substance Use, Occupation, and Mood) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s4:p0:c0-344]. Concretely:

1. An MLP classifier is trained on ~8 million EHR sentences (~340 million tokens) from the Research Patient Data Registry (RPDR) of the Partners HealthCare network [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000].
2. Sentences are automatically labeled for their risk factor domain(s) using a lexicon of clinician-identified domain-related keywords and multiword expressions, requiring no manual annotation; sentences are vectorized with the Universal Sentence Encoder (USE), a pretrained transformer attention network [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c1732-3263].
3. The topic-extraction component achieves an overall F1 of 0.828, and its output—counts of sentences per EHR involving each risk factor domain ('Baseline+Domain Sentences' model)—is fed into the readmission classifiers [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s12:p0:c0-2000].

Separately, sentences marked for one or more domains are passed to seven clinical sentiment MLP classifiers (trained on 3,500 clinician-labeled sentences with dropout 0.75 to prevent overfitting) whose outputs are averaged per domain into -1 to 1 sentiment scores [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c1732-3263].

Based on the currently visible excerpts, the paper does not report a direct numeric measure of "how much higher quality" the expert-annotated data is (e.g., a precision/recall delta of the annotations themselves). What it does provide:

- Qualitatively, the authors confirm that for specialized tasks, expert annotations are higher quality than crowd labels [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.07791:s16:p0:c0-1285]. Lay/crowd annotations have "high precision but low recall" relative to expert annotations, indicating crowd workers often miss target spans rather than producing false positives [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.07791:s0:p3:c0-935] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.07791:s23:p0:c3412-4563].
- Downstream quality is shown via model F1: models trained with expert-annotated data are "clearly superior" to those trained on the same amount of crowd labels, and an expert model trained on only 20% of the data beats a crowd model trained on all 5k abstracts [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.07791:s23:p0:c1737-3734] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.07791:s11:p4:c0-336].
- Routing the most-difficult instances to experts yields a 3.5 F1 improvement over crowd-only data (larger than adding a random set of expert annotations), and re-annotating the 600 most-difficult articles reaches 68.1% F1 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.07791:s12:p2:c0-1338] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.07791:s25:p0:c0-1998].

record.final_answer:
Based on the visible excerpts, the paper argues the adversarial setting is appropriate because adversarial misspellings are not merely academic but a real-world problem: spammers subtly misspell words to evade spam detection while preserving meaning, and internet censorship has led communities to adopt similar tricks to communicate surreptitiously [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s13:p0:c1709-3708]. Unlike adversarial attacks in computer vision, which are rarely encountered outside of academic research, misspellings genuinely occur in the wild [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s13:p0:c0-1998].

In this setting, rare and unseen words are particularly critical because they give attackers opportunities, so a reliable word recognizer must handle such cases gracefully rather than only performing well on in-vocabulary words [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s15:p0:c1702-3701]. Moreover, the attacks are realistic and impactful: an adversary can severely degrade text classifiers — e.g., a BERT sentiment model drops from 90.3% to 45.8% accuracy from a single adversarially-chosen character edit — motivating defenses like their word recognition model [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s12:p0:c0-980].

以下按题目顺序分别作答，不构成两篇论文的共同排序。

第一篇《Combating Adversarial Misspellings with Robust Word Recognition》(1905.11268):其评估的端任务是情感分析和复述检测(paraphrase detection),之所以选择这两个任务，是因为1-2个字符的编辑不会改变输出标签 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s8:p0:c0-148]。情感分类使用 BiLSTM 和微调 BERT,均在二分类的 Stanford Sentiment Treebank (SST) 上训练和评估 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s18:p0:c0-1999];摘要报告对抗攻击使 BERT 情感分析准确率从90.3%降至45.8%,其防御恢复至75% [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s12:p0:c0-980]。此外，其词识别(拼写纠错)模型也在 SST 电影评论上单独评估。该论文不涉及日语-越南语任务，可见证据中没有日越数据集的信息。

第二篇《Combining Advanced Methods in Japanese-Vietnamese Neural Machine Translation》(1805.07133):其端任务是构建首个日语↔越南语神经机器翻译系统 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1805.07133:s21:p0:c1698-3596]。所用的日越数据集是从 WIT3 语料中抽取的 TED 演讲日越平行数据，去除空行和重复后共106,758句对，验证集为 TED dev2010(568句)，测试集为 TED tst2010(1,220句)[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1805.07133:s8:p0:c0-264][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1805.07133:s20:p0:c0-2000]。用于反向翻译增强的还有 DongDu 的 VNESEcorpus 越南语单语数据(共349,578句，采样106,758句)[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1805.07133:s20:p0:c0-2000]。

record.final_answer: According to the paper, their BERT-based model can detect biases arising in the data collection and annotation process of hate speech datasets. Specifically, the authors found that misclassified tweets revealed sampling biases tied to dialect (e.g., African American Vernacular English) and geographic restriction (United States), where tweets containing disparage words such as "nigga", "faggot", "coon", or "queer" were oversampled and resulted in high rates of misclassification; these tweets were often annotated as hate/offensive by annotators without considering the social context of the tweeters (identity, dialect, geolocation), whereas they were actually merely offensive or even neither [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s20:p0:c1601-3521]. The abstract and conclusion state that "our model can capture some biases in data annotation and collection process" [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s10:p0:c0-1410], and that examining the results shows the model's ability to detect such collection/annotation biases, which the authors view as a clue for using pre-trained BERT to debias hate speech datasets in future work [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s9:p0:c0-1312] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s13:p0:c0-1999].

- Sampling/collection bias: Waseem et al. used a small ad-hoc keyword set and Davidson et al. used the crowdsourced Hatebase lexicon to sample tweets, which introduced biases into the collected data [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s8:p2:c0-2000].
- Racial/dialect and geographic bias in the Davidson dataset: tweets in African American Vernacular English and geographically restricted (U.S.) content are oversampled—e.g., tweets containing slurs like "nigga", "faggot", "coon", or "queer"—leading to high misclassification rates [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s8:p2:c0-2000].
- Annotation bias: annotators labeled many tweets containing disrespectful words as hate/offensive without considering the speaker's social context, identity, or dialect, when those tweets were merely offensive or neither; their model can correctly discriminate such tweets (e.g., tweets with implicit hatred or "neither" cases), which the authors attribute to BERT's pre-trained general knowledge [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s8:p2:c0-2000].

The authors say this ability to detect biases in dataset collection/annotation is a valuable clue for using pre-trained BERT to debias hate speech datasets in future work [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s9:p0:c0-1312].

record.final_answer: On their constructed divorce-proceedings dataset (100,000 real case documents from China Judgments Online — 80,000 train / 10,000 validation / 10,000 test, with 185,723 valid pleas, ~52% supported), their AutoJudge model achieved the best results: P=80.4, R=86.6, F1=83.4, Acc=82.2 (averaged over 10 runs), outperforming all baselines including lexical-feature SVM (Acc 55.5), neural text classifiers such as CNN (77.6) and GRU+Attention (79.1), and RC models such as AoA (78.3) and r-net (78.4) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s25:p0:c0-1926]. Key findings: (1) simply concatenating law articles (CNN/GRU+law) hurts performance, while integrating law articles with attention improves it, supporting the importance of modeling interactions among fact descriptions, pleas, and law articles [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s25:p0:c0-1926]; (2) ablation tests show each component (attentive reader, law articles, CNN output layer, legal prior preprocessing) contributes, and using ground-truth law articles boosts performance by several points in both F1 and Acc, though this is unattainable in real-world automatic prediction [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s15:p5:c0-1209]; (3) attention visualization shows interpretability, and failure analysis attributes most errors to government anonymization of critical case elements such as explicit dates [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s26:p0:c1693-3657].

record.final_answer: On their constructed dataset — a large-scale real-world set of 100,000 civil case documents from the Supreme People's Court of China [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s20:p0:c1665-3663] — the authors train and evaluate AutoJudge and several baselines. Main results (Table 1, %): AutoJudge achieves P=80.4, R=86.6, F1=83.4, Acc=82.2, outperforming all baselines including SVM (F1 55.6), CNN (F1 79.0), GRU (F1 76.1), GRU+Attention (F1 80.0), AoA (F1 79.2), and r-net (F1 79.2) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s25:p0:c0-1926]. They report significant improvement over previous methods and off-the-shelf state-of-the-art models under both classification and question-answering frameworks [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s20:p0:c1665-3663]. Ablation tests (Table 2) further support robustness: removing the reading mechanism drops F1 to 78.9 (↓4.5) and Acc to 78.2 (↓4.0); removing law articles gives F1 79.6 (↓3.8), Acc 78.4 (↓3.8); replacing CNN with LSTM gives F1 77.6; while using ground-truth law articles improves to F1 85.1 (↑1.7), Acc 84.1 (↑1.9) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s25:p0:c1634-3572]. Overall, the experiments (on divorce proceedings) show AutoJudge achieves considerable improvement over all baselines, with attention visualization and failure analysis noting the anonymity issue as the most common cause of errors [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.06537:s26:p0:c1693-3657].

record.final_answer:
The paper does not train content selection in isolation; instead, the selection mask β is treated as a latent variable and trained jointly with generation via amortized variational inference [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s19:p0:c0-1996]. Specifically:

- The selector and generator are co-trained within the same objective by maximizing the marginal data likelihood, so the selector can automatically explore selecting strategies that best fit the generator [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s20:p0:c0-1927].
- Since the exact marginal likelihood log E_{β∼B(γ)} pθ(Y|X,β) is intractable, the model is trained end-to-end by maximizing a lower bound of the marginal likelihood, without human selection annotations; ground-truth selections are unknown during training [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s17:p0:c0-901] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s20:p0:c0-1927].
- A learned posterior qφ(β|X,Y) is used in the variational framework [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s25:p0:c0-1853].
- The objective includes a hyperparameter ϵ that constrains an upper bound on the conditional mutual information I(β,Y|X) via a KL penalty term (Eq. 5), adjusting the performance/controllability trade-off [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s21:p0:c2926-4272] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s0:p3:c0-1017].

This contrasts with Bottom-up (heuristic targets, independent training), Soft-select (deterministic mask), and Reinforce-select (high-variance RL) alternatives discussed in the paper [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s19:p0:c0-1996] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s8:p0:c0-1341].

record.final_answer:
The paper describes content selection as part of an end-to-end trainable model rather than a standalone selection-only training procedure, and the visible excerpts support the following:

- Content selection is treated as latent variables and trained with amortized variational inference, which gives lower training variance than reinforcement-learning-based selection; the selector and generator are co-trained within the same objective, and the framework is task-agnostic and can be inserted into any encoder-decoder architecture [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s19:p0:c0-1996][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s0:p3:c0-1017].
- The model can be trained end-to-end without human annotations by maximizing a lower bound of the marginal likelihood [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s18:p0:c0-1999].
- Training uses only source–text pairs; the ground-truth content selection for each pair is unknown, so selection is learned as a latent variable rather than from selection labels [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s20:p0:c0-1927].

If by "only content selection" you mean training the selector alone, the paper does discuss such an approach (the "Bottom-up" baseline): the selector is trained to target heuristically extracted contents (e.g., overlapped source–target words, high tf-idf sentences, or image objects appearing in the caption), while a standard encoder-decoder model is trained independently; at test time the selector's prediction hard-masks the attention to guide generation [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s20:p0:c0-1927]. The paper notes drawbacks: heuristic contents may be coarse, and independently trained selector and decoder may not adapt to each other [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.04453:s20:p0:c0-1927].

In short: the paper's own approach trains selection jointly with generation end-to-end (latent-variable, amortized variational inference, lower-bound maximization), while selection-only training corresponds to the Bottom-up baseline with heuristic targets. Details beyond what these excerpts show (e.g., full optimization procedures) cannot be confirmed from the visible text.

In short: the paper's own approach trains selection jointly with generation end-to-end (latent-variable, amortized variational inference, lower-bound maximization), while selection-only training corresponds to the Bottom-up baseline with heuristic targets. record.final_answer: The paper explains BT's effectiveness mainly through the properties of the artificial (back-translated) source data (§3.2). Compared with natural sources, artificial sources are (i) on average shorter; (ii) aligned more monotonically with the target (e.g., lower Kendall τ of alignments), which the authors call "a facilitating factor for NMT" [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s24:p0:c0-1998]; (iii) syntactically simpler (differences in tree-depth distributions); and (iv) distributionally more concentrated in word occurrences, with fewer rare events. Their intuition is that properties (i) and (ii) help translation relative to natural sources, while (iv) is detrimental; they verified the regularity property by selecting natural parallel data based on word-alignment regularity, which proved preferable and "might explain that the mostly monotonic BT from Moses are almost as good as the fluid BT from NMT and that both boost the baseline" [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s24:p0:c1732-2944]. Relatedly, they note BT acts mainly on the decoder side — "BT impacts most of all the decoder" [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s17:p1:c0-497] — and that artificial data with easier examples actually encourages overfitting rather than acting as a regularizer [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s24:p0:c0-1998]. Note that the full abstract-level synthesis of all their explanations may extend beyond the retrieved excerpts, but the §3.2 property analysis above is directly visible evidence.

record.final_answer: In this paper, the effectiveness of back-translation (BT) is explained through a linguistic and distributional analysis of the artificial (back-translated) source sentences compared with natural sources (Section 3.2). They observe four properties: (i) artificial sources are on average shorter than natural ones; (ii) their word alignments tend to be more monotonic (measured by Kendall τ), which the authors note is a facilitating factor for NMT; (iii) syntactically, artificial sources are simpler than real data; and (iv) their word occurrences are distributionally more concentrated [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s24:p0:c0-1998]. Their intuition is that the shorter length and more monotonic alignments help translation relative to natural sources (while the distributional concentration is detrimental), and they verify that selecting natural data by alignment regularity improves performance — which they say may explain why the mostly monotonic BT from Moses is almost as good as NMT-generated BT and why both boost the baseline [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s24:p0:c1732-2944]. Additionally, they argue BT is not acting as a regularizer in their domain-adaptation setting: learning curves show the BT-trained system improves quickly then plateaus, so “BT does not help to avoid overfitting, it actually encourages it, which may be due “easier” training examples” (referring back to the properties above) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s4:p8:c0-649]. In short: BT works because its artificial sources are easier to translate — shorter, more monotonic, and syntactically simpler — not because it regularizes the model. (The abstract likewise states the study gives new explanations as to why BT is the case [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s20:p0:c0-935]; the property analysis above is the explanation visible in this retrieval.)

**1) Decoder architecture:** The system is an encoder–decoder over character sequences, and the decoder is an LSTM decoder that generates the output word form character by character, conditioned on the encoder states via an attention mechanism [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.01541:s13:p0:c0-1782]. The overall approach is a character-level encoder–decoder architecture with three innovations: a wide context window (full-sentence LSTM context encoding), multi-task learning with an auxiliary MSD-prediction decoder, and multilingual training [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.01541:s12:p0:c0-1972] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.01541:s12:p0:c1731-3632].

**2) Type of inflections considered:** The paper addresses morphological (re)inflection *in context* — i.e., universal morphological reinflection, Task 2 of CoNLL–SIGMORPHON 2018, where an inflected word form must be generated given a lemma and the context it occurs in. This contrasts with previous SIGMORPHON tasks, which were context-agnostic [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.01541:s12:p0:c0-1972]. The task has two tracks: Track 1 provides context word forms, lemmas, and morphosyntactic descriptions (MSD), while Track 2 provides only word forms [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.01541:s12:p0:c0-1972]. The auxiliary MSD prediction covers nouns, adjectives, and verbs [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1809.01541:s16:p0:c0-1995].

record.final_answer: The paper explains BT's effectiveness by analyzing the properties of back-translated (artificial) source sentences compared to natural sources. They observe that artificial sources: (i) contain more regular/common word patterns, (ii) have more regular word alignments, (iii) are syntactically simpler (differing tree-depth distributions), and (iv) have more concentrated word distributions with fewer rare events [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s24:p0:c1732-2944]. Their intuition is that properties (i) and (ii) help translation relative to natural sources — which also explains why the mostly monotonic BT from Moses is almost as good as the more fluent BT from NMT, and why both boost the baseline [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s24:p0:c1732-2944]. The abstract confirms the study provides "new explanations as to why this is the case" for BT's effectiveness [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s20:p0:c0-935].

以下分别回答两篇论文的问题，不做跨论文排名比较。

**1）《Using Monolingual Data in Neural Machine Translation: a Systematic Study》（1903.11437）：数据是什么语言的？**
该研究的单语数据为**英语**，来自 WMT 2017 共享任务的全部英语单语数据，约 1.74 亿句 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s4:p2:c0-296]，应用于英语—法语和英语—德语两个翻译方向 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1903.11437:s22:p0:c0-1826]。

**2）《To lemmatize or not to lemmatize…》（1909.03135）：为什么英语中不需要词形还原？**
论文的实验表明，这一假设"indeed true for languages with simple morphology (like English)"（对像英语这样形态简单的语言确实成立）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.03135:s6:p1:c0-691]；而在形态丰富的语言（如俄语）中，基于词元（lemma）的模型能更好地处理多种词形变化，才能带来提升 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.03135:s6:p1:c0-691]。此外，ELMo 完全基于字符的词表示（字符序列上的卷积层）能够自行学习处理拼写和形态变化，并避免未登录词问题，因此其作者建议除分词外不做任何规范化 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.03135:s1:p0:c0-631]。

**1) 《A Joint Model for Multimodal Document Quality Assessment》(1901.01010)**
- **数据集规模**：使用两个数据集。Wikipedia 数据集共 29,794 篇文章（从 FA、GA、B、C、Start、Stub 六个质量类别各抽样 5,000 篇，按 8:1:1 划分为 24,000 训练 / 3,000 开发 / 2,794 测试）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1901.01010:s7:p1:c0-493]；arXiv 数据集共 11,778 篇论文，分三个 CS 子集：cs.ai 4,092、cs.cl 2,638、cs.lg 5,048 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1901.01010:s19:p0:c1757-3555]。
- **训练时间**：可见证据中未给出明确的训练时长数字，故无法回答该点（部分受限）。

**2) 《Sentence-BERT》(1908.10084)**
- **数据集规模**：主要训练数据为 SNLI（57 万句对）与 MultiNLI（43 万句对）的组合，用 3-way softmax 分类目标微调一个 epoch，batch size 为 16 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1908.10084:s3:p0:c0-583]。
- **训练时间**：由于只微调预训练的 BERT/RoBERTa 而非从头训练，SBERT 可在不到 20 分钟内完成调优 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1908.10084:s1:p5:c0-392]。

- **Sanders and HCR datasets**: an ensemble of base classifiers (ENS with NB, Random Forest, SVM, Logistic Regression) from [15], combined with bag-of-words (BoW), feature hashing, and lexicons — also state-of-the-art on those datasets [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.08032:s17:p0:c3101-4588].

The proposed model achieved 86.63 accuracy on STS, outperforming all baselines [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.08032:s9:p0:c0-463].

record.final_answer:
In 1604.05781, causal statements were selected from a 10% sample of Twitter posts made during 2013 (Gardenhose API), using the following criteria:

- Only English-language tweets were kept: user-reported language 'English', plus tweets matching more English stopwords (NLTK) than any other language's set.
- Retweets were excluded.
- Text was preprocessed: punctuation, XML characters, hyperlinks, at-mentions and hashtags removed; documents tokenized on whitespace.
- A causal document had to contain exactly one occurrence of the exact unigrams 'caused', 'causing', or 'causes' — 'cause' was excluded because it is a popular contraction for 'because'; the one-cause-word restriction keeps the analysis to single relationships between two relata.
- Documents containing bidirectional words ('associate', 'relate', 'connect', 'correlate', and their stems) were also excluded, since the focus is causality rather than mere association.

This yielded roughly 1M causal statements, with a matched random control corpus controlling for time of year [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1604.05781:s11:p0:c0-1993] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1604.05781:s6:p0:c0-555].

两篇论文分别回答如下，不涉及统一排名：

**1705.09665《Community Identity and User Engagement in a Multi-Community Landscape》——如何度量社区的时间动态性（dynamicity）？**

作者先在词层面定义波动性（volatility），即词 w 在时刻 t 于社区 c 中的 PMI（相对于该社区的全部历史）：Vct(w) = log Pct(w)/PcT(w)；若词在某一时间窗口中出现频率高于整个历史，则被视为“波动”词（类似短期时尚）。词级度量随后扩展到整条发言（取词的平均），最后社区层面的动态性被定义为该社区内所有发言的平均波动性——高度动态的社区会不断在不同时间窗口间转换兴趣，反映为波动的语言；语言长期相对一致的社区则被称为“稳定”（stable）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c1821-3568] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s3:p0:c0-471]。

**1604.05781《What we write about when we write about causality》——“因果陈述”的筛选标准是什么？**

- 数据来自 2013 年 Twitter 的 10% 均匀样本（Gardenhose API）；只保留英语推文（用户报告语言为英语，且匹配的英语停用词多于其他语言的停用词集，NLTK 词表）；排除转推。
- 文本预处理：去除标点、XML 字符、超链接、@提及和话题标签。
- 因果文档必须恰好包含一次精确的因果词 'caused'、'causing' 或 'causes'——不含 'cause'（因其常被用作 'because' 的缩略语）；每个文档只允许一个因果词，以保证只分析两个对象之间的单一因果关系。
- 排除含有双向词（'associate'、'relate'、'connect'、'correlate' 及其词干）的文档，因为研究焦点是因果而非关联。

由此得到约 100 万条因果陈述，并配有按时间年份控制的随机对照语料 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1604.05781:s11:p0:c0-1993] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1604.05781:s6:p0:c0-555]。

（一）《Community Identity and User Engagement in a Multi-Community Landscape》（1705.09665）：如何衡量一个社区的“时间动态性”？
作者在社区层面将动态性（dynamicity）定义为该社区内所有话语的平均波动性（volatility）：高度动态的社区会不断从一个时间窗口转向另一个时间窗口地改变兴趣，这种时序变化反映在其易变语言的使用上；语言在时间上相对一致的社区则被称为稳定（stable）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s4:p2:c0-396]。其底层是词级度量：对词 w 在社区 c 的时期 t，波动性定义为相对整个历史 cT 的 PMI，即 Vct(w) = log(Pct(w)/PcT(w))；若某词在某时期出现频率高于其整体历史频率，则该词是“波动的”（类似短期风尚），若跨时间频率接近不变（V 接近 0）则为“稳定”；话语层面的波动性由其中各词的平均得出 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s17:p0:c1821-3568]。

record.final_answer: The selection criteria were: (1) the document must contain exactly one occurrence of the exact unigrams 'caused', 'causing', or 'causes' ('cause' was excluded because it is often a contraction of 'because'); (2) limiting to one cause-word per document restricted analysis to a single relationship between two relata; and (3) documents containing bidirectional words ('associate', 'relate', 'connect', 'correlate' and their stems) were excluded, since causality is an inherently one-sided relationship. Synonyms of the cause-words were not considered. Control documents contained none of these words, were matched in number per fifteen-minute period during 2013, and were otherwise randomly selected. 【1705.09665《Community Identity and User Engagement in a Multi-Community Landscape》：如何衡量社区的时间动态性？】

【1604.05781《What we write about when we write about causality...》："因果陈述"的筛选标准是什么？】
筛选"因果文档"的标准是：(1) 文档中恰好出现一次精确词元 'caused'、'causing' 或 'causes'（不含 'cause'，因为它常被用作 'because' 的缩略形式）；(2) 每篇文档只含一个因果词，从而将分析限定为两个实体间的单一因果关系；(3) 排除含双向词（'associate'、'relate'、'connect'、'correlate' 及其词干）的文档，因为因果是单向关系；因果词的同义词也未纳入。对照组文档则不含任何因果词和双向词，在2013年每15分钟时段内数量与因果文档匹配，其余随机选取，最终得到965,560篇因果文档和965,560篇对照文档 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1604.05781:s1:p2:c0-1268]。

record.final_answer:
Their offensive speech classifier (a 100-estimator entropy-based random forest over word-embedding-derived hate-vector similarity scores) performed as follows [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s10:p0:c1739-3739]:

- 10-fold cross-validation on the training/validation set: Random Forest achieved 92.0% accuracy and 91.9% F1-score, outperforming Decision Tree (91.8%/91.4%), Naive Bayes (81.5%/81.2%), and Stochastic Gradient Descent (80.7%/80.0%) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s10:p0:c3504-4471].
- Real-world holdout set evaluation: accuracy of 89.6% and F1-score of 89.2%, indicating robustness against over-fitting [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s4:p2:c0-445].
- On high-confidence samples, precision exceeded 95% and recall exceeded 85%, suggesting the classifier tends to underestimate offensive speech, so reported offensiveness levels are a lower bound [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s4:p7:c0-308].
- Varying holdout set sizes and confidence thresholds showed that beyond a fairly low threshold, dataset size had little impact on accuracy, precision, or recall [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s11:p0:c0-2000].

- 10-fold cross-validation on the training/validation set: Random Forest achieved 92.0% accuracy and 91.9% F1-score, outperforming Decision Tree (91.8%/91.4%), Naive Bayes (81.5%/81.2%), and Stochastic Gradient Descent (80.7%/80.0%) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s10:p0:c3504-4471].
- Real-world holdout set evaluation: accuracy of 89.6% and F1-score of 89.2%, indicating robustness against over-fitting [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s4:p2:c0-445].
- On high-confidence samples, precision exceeded 95% and recall exceeded 85%, suggesting the classifier tends to underestimate offensive speech, so reported offensiveness levels are a lower bound [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s4:p7:c0-308].
- Varying holdout set sizes and confidence thresholds showed that beyond a fairly low threshold, dataset size had little impact on accuracy, precision, or recall [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1706.01875:s11:p0:c0-2000].

record.final_answer:
根据源证据，论文 1611.08661 中使用的基准如下：

- **主要基准 (Link Prediction)：TransE**。作者明确指出：“我们的基准是 TransE，因为我们的模型的得分函数是基于 TransE 的”，并且所提出的联合模型 (CBOW, LSTM, A-LSTM) 在所有指标上均优于 TransE [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.08661:s19:p0:c0-1670]。TransE 也作为链接预测中头实体/尾实体预测分类别的对比基准出现 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.08661:s19:p0:c0-1670]。

- **三元组分类基准**：比较表包括 TransE、TransH、TransR、CTransR、TransD 和 TranSparse，它们与 Jointly(NBOW)、Jointly(LSTM) 和 Jointly(A-LSTM) 在 WN18 和 FB15K 上进行了对比 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.08661:s20:p0:c0-1904]。

- **参考先进模型**：在 FB15K 上的链接预测中，论文指出他们的模型在 Hits@10 指标上不如最先进的 TransD，但注意到他们的得分函数是基于 TransE 而非 TransD，并且他们的方法可以与其他最先进的嵌入模型（如 TransD）结合使用 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.08661:s19:p0:c0-1670]。

- 在所有关系映射类型（1-to-1, 1-to-N, N-to-1, N-to-N）中，模型的表现也优于基准 TransE [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.08661:s10:p11:c0-313]。

record.final_answer: Partially. The paper's Italian Word2Vec embeddings are not tested on a downstream NLP task (e.g., classification or tagging); instead they are evaluated intrinsically on an analogy benchmark: a test of 19,791 analogies split into semantic and syntactic categories, where the model must guess a word like 'queen' from 'man : woman = king : b*' [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:2001.09332:s14:p0:c0-1886]. Accuracy is computed with two vector-arithmetic metrics, 3COSADD and 3COSMUL [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:2001.09332:s14:p0:c1605-2608], and their model is compared against Tipodis [10] and Berardi [11] models, achieving e.g. 53–54% total accuracy versus ~44–51% for the baselines [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:2001.09332:s17:p0:c0-1998]. So while the abstract frames word representation as fundamental for NLP tasks [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:2001.09332:s9:p0:c0-584], the evaluation itself is limited to analogy tests rather than an application-level NLP task.

The trained model is compared against two prior Italian W2V models (Tipodis [10] and Berardi [11]), with accuracy reported separately on semantic and syntactic analogies (e.g., total accuracy of ~54.63% with 3COSMUL against Berardi's model) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:2001.09332:s17:p0:c0-1998]. While no broad NLP applications (e.g., classification or translation) are evaluated in the visible excerpts, the analogy test is a standard intrinsic NLP evaluation of word embeddings.

For "Prose for a Painting" (1910.03634):

- **Painting embedding / poem generation**: The paper uses an actor-critic architecture with **3 parallel CNNs** (an object CNN, a sentiment CNN, and a scene CNN) for feature extraction from the painting, feeding an **RNN generator** (as an agent), with **2 discriminators** providing feedback to the agent for model improvement [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s14:p0:c0-1999] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c0-2000].

- **Language style transfer**: A **seq2seq model with global attention** transfers the generated poem into Shakespearean prose; a seq2seq model **with pointer networks** was also tried, but global attention performed better (average target BLEU 29.65 vs. 26.97) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c0-2000] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s16:p0:c0-1997].

SBERT 是在预训练的 BERT/RoBERTa 网络基础上微调，训练时间少于 20 分钟 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1908.10084:s1:p5:c0-392]。

- 画作嵌入/诗歌生成：采用 actor-critic 架构，使用 3 个并行 CNN（物体 CNN、情感 CNN、场景 CNN）提取画作特征，输入一个作为智能体的 RNN 生成器，并由 2 个判别器提供反馈以改进模型 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s14:p0:c0-1999] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c0-2000]。

两篇论文分别回答如下（不进行任何统一排名）：

1）训练时间（Sentence-BERT, 1908.10084）：由于只对预训练的 BERT/RoBERTa 进行微调，SBERT 的训练可在不到 20 分钟内完成，且效果优于可比的句子嵌入方法 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1908.10084:s1:p5:c0-392]。（对比：原始 BERT 仅在 1 万句中找最相似句对就需约 65 小时，而 SBERT 只需约 5 秒 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1908.10084:s14:p0:c0-1130]。）

2）画作嵌入与语言风格迁移模型（Prose for a Painting, 1910.03634）：画作特征提取使用 3 个 CNN，并由 RNN 生成器（作为智能体）结合 2 个判别器通过策略梯度的多对抗训练生成英文诗歌 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c0-2000]；语言风格迁移（现代英语→莎士比亚文风）使用带全局注意力的 seq2seq 模型（另尝试了带指针网络的 seq2seq，但全局注意力模型效果更好，BLEU 29.65 对 26.97）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c1707-2869]。

按要求分别回答两篇论文（不推断共同排名）：

record.final_answer:
According to "Prose for a Painting" (1910.03634), the pipeline uses two model groups:

Painting embedding / feature extraction: For generating an English poem from a painting, the authors use an existing actor-critic architecture with 3 parallel CNNs — an object CNN, a sentiment CNN, and a scene CNN — for feature extraction; these features are combined with a skip-thought model providing poetic clues and fed into a CNN-RNN generator (agent) trained by policy gradient with 2 discriminator networks as rewards [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s3:p0:c0-1079] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s14:p0:c0-1999].

Language style transfer (modern English poem → Shakespearean prose): A sequence-to-sequence model with a single-layer unidirectional LSTM encoder and single-layer LSTM decoder, using pre-trained retrofitted word embeddings (dimension 192) shared between source and target [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s14:p0:c1738-3737] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c1707-2869]. Two attention variants were compared: seq2seq with global attention (best, BLEU 29.65) and seq2seq with pointer networks (BLEU 26.97) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.03634:s15:p0:c0-2000].

record.final_answer: Multi-agent dual learning (MADL) extends standard dual learning, which exploits the duality between a primal task (X→Y) and dual task (Y→X), by using multiple primal and dual models instead of just one. Specifically, it uses N pre-trained primal translation models f_i (X→Y) and N pre-trained dual translation models g_j (Y→X), each with non-negative hyper-parameter weights α_i and β_j summing to 1. These are combined into weighted ensemble models F_α (X→Y) and G_β (Y→X), which translate by maximizing the weighted sum of log-probabilities from the individual models. MADL is then trained with a joint objective: the bilingual translation losses of the final models f_0 and g_0 on the bilingual dataset B, plus monolingual reconstruction terms that feed monolingual data M_x and M_y through the combined models (y | F_α(G_β(y)) and x | G_β(F_α(x))). For inference, MADL outputs a single final primal model f_0 and a single final dual model g_0 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s34:p0:c0-1887].

record.final_answer: Multi-agent dual learning (MADL) is an enhanced version of dual learning that leverages the duality between the primal task (X→Y) and the dual task (Y→X) to boost both tasks. Instead of a single pair of models, it uses N primal translation models fi (X→Y) and N dual translation models gj (Y→X), all pre-trained on bilingual data, and eventually outputs one f0 and one g0 for inference [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s34:p0:c0-1887]. Each primal model fi gets a non-negative weight αi and each dual model gj a non-negative weight βj (all hyper-parameters summing to 1), which combine into a combined translation model Fα from X to Y and Gβ from Y to X; for translation, Fα(x) picks the ŷ maximizing the weighted sum of αi·log P(ỹ|x; fi) over the agents (and similarly for Gβ in the reverse direction) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277]. The training objective combines likelihood on the bilingual dataset B for f0 and g0 with reconstruction losses on monolingual data Mx and My: minimizing −log P(x|Gβ(Fα(x))) on Mx and −log P(y|Fα(Gβ(y))) on My, i.e., round-trip translation through the combined primal and dual models should reconstruct the original monolingual sentence [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277]. MADL was integrated into the submitted WMT19 systems [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s34:p0:c0-1887].

record.final_answer:
Multi-agent dual learning (MADL) is described in Section 2.1 of the paper as an enhanced version of dual learning [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277]. Core idea: dual learning exploits the duality between a primal task (translation X→Y) and a dual task (Y→X) to boost both; MADL extends this by introducing multiple primal and dual models instead of just one pair [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s34:p0:c0-1887].

How it works:
- It uses N primal translation models f_i (X→Y) and N dual translation models g_j (Y→X), all pre-trained on bilingual data. Each model gets a non-negative hyper-parameter weight (α_i for primal, β_j for dual, weights summing to 1), forming combined models F_α and G_β. At inference time a translation is produced by maximizing the weighted sum of the models' log-probabilities (i.e., a weighted ensemble) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277].
- The training objective minimizes likelihood on the bilingual data for the two main models (f_0, g_0), plus dual-reconstruction terms on monolingual data: for x in monolingual X, translate with F_α then back-translate with G_β and maximize log P(x | G_β(F_α(x))); symmetrically for monolingual y using F_α(G_β(y)) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s35:p0:c0-1277].
- In practice (e.g., the English↔German system), F_α is the combination of f_0 and two other models with equal weights and G_β similarly; during training only f_0 and g_0 are updated, using sampled monolingual data to speed up training [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s12:p3:c0-591].
- Effectiveness: on English→German, back-translation boosted BLEU from 45.6 to 47.4 on news18, and MADL further boosted it to 50.4 (about 3 additional points) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s13:p0:c0-690]. Notably, their German→French submission was a single system trained by MADL, achieving 37.3 BLEU and first place [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1911.06191:s14:p3:c0-351].

record.final_answer:
On their new dataset (180K+ recipes, 700K+ user interactions/reviews), the personalized models outperformed the non-personalized baselines:

- Perplexity: All personalized models beat the Encoder-Decoder baseline in BPE perplexity, with 'Prior Name' best (9.516 vs 9.611 for Enc-Dec; Prior Recipe 9.551, Prior Tech 9.572) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.00105:s4:p1:c0-1134][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.00105:s13:p0:c0-1776].
- BLEU/ROUGE: Personalized models were comparable to the baseline; they scored better on BLEU-1 (more ingredient entities present) but worse on BLEU-4 because personalized recipes deviate from the gold text at the phrase level; the authors argue BLEU/ROUGE are not appropriate for generation quality [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.00105:s4:p2:c0-435].
- Diversity: Personalized models produced more diverse recipes (higher Distinct-1/2) than the baseline (e.g., Prior Tech D-1 0.233 vs Enc-Dec 0.220) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.00105:s13:p0:c0-1776].
- Personalization metrics: User Matching Accuracy and MRR were much higher for personalized models, best for 'Prior Name' (UMA 0.505, MRR 0.628 vs baseline 0.100/0.293) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.00105:s13:p0:c0-1776].
- Coherence: Personalized models achieved recipe-level coherence scores of 1.78–1.82 vs the baseline's 1.77, and step entailment scores up to 0.78 vs 0.72 for the baseline [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.00105:s14:p0:c1727-3727].
- Human evaluation: Evaluators preferred personalized outputs over baseline 63% of the time (pairwise comparisons over 310 recipe pairs), and 60% of users in a smaller survey found personalized recipes more coherent and preferable [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.00105:s14:p0:c1727-3727].

Overall, the experiments confirmed that personalization from historical user preferences helps generate plausible, diverse, and user-aligned recipes from incomplete ingredients.

record.final_answer: The authors point to their error analysis of misclassified samples. They observe that many errors are due to biases from data collection and annotation rules rather than the classifier itself: Waseem et al. sampled tweets with a small ad-hoc set of keywords and Davidson et al. used the crowdsourced Hatebase lexicon, introducing biases into the collected data; in the Davidson dataset, tweets written in African American Vernacular English with geographic restriction to the USA were oversampled (e.g., containing words like “nigga”, “faggot”, “coon”, “queer”), leading to high misclassification rates [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s8:p2:c0-2000]. However, they argue these misclassifications reflect annotator behavior—annotators labeled samples with disrespectful words as hate or offensive without considering the social context of the tweeter (speaker identity or dialect)—rather than low classifier performance. They cite specific examples: tweets IDs 6, 8, and 10 contain offensive words/slurs that are not hate or offensive in all cases (used in daily communication), while tweets IDs 3, 4, and 9 show their BERT-based classifier can correctly discriminate tweets without or with implicit hatred content, which they attribute to the general knowledge learned from pre-training on normal corpora [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s8:p2:c0-2000]. Based on this, they conclude that examining the results shows the model's ability to detect some biases in the process of collecting or annotating datasets, which could be valuable for debiasing hate speech datasets in future studies [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s0:p6:c0-512] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.12574:s9:p0:c0-1312].

record.final_answer: The paper incorporates sentiment analysis as part of an NLP feature-extraction pipeline over EHR free text. Sentences from admission notes are labeled for seven risk factor domains (Appearance, Thought Process, Thought Content, Interpersonal, Substance Use, Occupation, Mood) using a lexicon of clinician-identified keywords [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000]. Sentences are vectorized with the Universal Sentence Encoder (USE), and those marked for one or more domains are passed to seven clinical sentiment MLP classifiers (one per domain), trained on 3,500 clinician-labeled EHR sentences with two hidden layers and 0.75 dropout to avoid overfitting [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c1732-3263]. Each domain's model outputs are averaged across notes into a single -1 to 1 score of the patient's functioning level [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c1732-3263]. These clinical sentiment scores, together with the relative sentence counts per risk domain, are used as unstructured features alongside structured variables in the readmission classifier; the sentiment features produced the best results (F1 = 0.72) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s12:p0:c3366-4547].

Based on the currently visible excerpts, the paper incorporates sentiment analysis as follows (details of the exact pipeline are not fully visible in the retrieved text):

- They augment traditional structured-feature-based readmission classifiers with NLP-based features derived from free-text EHR narratives, including clinical sentiment analysis alongside topic extraction [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s8:p0:c0-675][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s9:p0:c1710-3707].
- Clinical sentiment features are computed for each of seven risk domains and are extracted via an NLP pipeline applied to a corpus of 2,346 clinical notes (admission notes, progress notes, and discharge summaries) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s9:p0:c1710-3707][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s12:p0:c3366-4547].
- The approach is described as a hybrid machine learning method combining deep learning (state-of-the-art MLP methods) to generate clinically meaningful sentiment features that feed into downstream linear models for interpretable predictions [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s12:p0:c3366-4547].
- They compare a structured-variables-only baseline against models incorporating these free-text-derived sentiment features; the clinical sentiment features outperformed the baseline on all evaluation metrics (F1 = 0.72) [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s9:p0:c1710-3707][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s12:p0:c3366-4547].

record.final_answer:
The paper incorporates sentiment analysis as an NLP-derived unstructured feature set for predicting 30-day psychiatric readmission:

1. **Seven risk-factor domains**: Free-text EHR narratives (admission notes, progress notes, discharge summaries) are analyzed with respect to seven risk factor domains previously linked to readmission risk — Appearance, Thought Process, Thought Content, Interpersonal, Substance Use, Occupation, and Mood [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000].
2. **Clinical sentiment scores per domain**: For each of these domains, the pipeline computes clinical sentiment scores evaluating the patient's psychosocial functioning as positive, negative, or neutral; these are computed for every note in the admission, alongside the relative number of sentences involving each domain [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000].
3. **Automatic pipeline**: The scores come from an automatic topic-extraction and sentiment-analysis pipeline from the authors' prior work (Holderness et al., 2019), pretrained on in-house psychiatric EHR text, achieving ~0.828 F1 on topic extraction and 0.5 F1 on the clinical sentiment component. It uses a multilayer perceptron (MLP) trained on ~8 million EHR sentences (~340 million tokens) from the Partners HealthCare Research Patient Data Registry [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s11:p0:c0-2000].
4. **Use in the model**: These sentiment features are combined with structured clinical variables in a downstream model, and the authors report that domain-level clinical sentiment features extracted from free-text narratives further improve early readmission prediction [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1910.04006:s6:p2:c0-728].

record.final_answer:
The paper (1705.09665) answers this by mapping ~300 Reddit communities onto a language-based typology defined by two identity dimensions—distinctiveness (how "niche" a community's interests are) and dynamicity (how volatile those interests are over time)—and then showing how social phenomena systematically vary across that landscape.

**Retention:** Engagement and retention depend strongly and systematically on the identity type. Dynamic communities that continually renew their discussion content have substantially higher monthly retention (Spearman's ρ = 0.70), and distinctive communities show moderately higher retention than generic ones (ρ = 0.33). However, niche communities engender strong focused interest that does not necessarily translate into long-term retention [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s19:p0:c1663-3663].

**Acculturation:** The acculturation gap (the linguistic divide between engaged and non-engaged users) varies with identity type: it is most pronounced in stable, highly distinctive communities. At the other extreme, in generic communities like pics or worldnews there is no distinctive linguistic identity for newcomers to adopt [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s20:p0:c1724-3724].

**Content affinity (specificity and volatility gaps):** In nearly all communities (94%) active users engage with more community-specific content than outsiders, but the magnitude varies greatly (e.g., a strong divide in Homebrewing vs. almost none in funny). Both the specificity gap (ρ = 0.34) and volatility gap (ρ = 0.53) correlate strongly with distinctiveness. Notably, in niche communities established members engage more with volatile content than outsiders, whereas in generic communities the opposite holds—outsiders engage more with volatile content, perhaps as an entry point to the community [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s21:p0:c3415-5413][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s0:p10:c0-808].

Overall, the paper concludes that radically contrasting engagement patterns emerge in different regions of the identity landscape, and this variation can be partly explained by the type of collective identity each community fosters—so phenomena like retention, acculturation, and content affinity are highly contingent on community type, which is consequential for community maintainers [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s12:p1:c0-702][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s22:p0:c3361-5354].

record.final_answer: The paper introduces a language-based typology of community identity—how distinctive and how temporally dynamic it is—and shows that social phenomena (user engagement measures) manifest differently across community types: distinctive, dynamic ("niche") communities retain users better but show larger acculturation gaps between newcomers and established members [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s14:p0:c0-1444][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s0:p9:c0-531]. The typology explains cross-community variation in retention, acculturation, and content affinity, and the patterns can even reverse by community type: in niche communities established members are more likely to engage with volatile content than outsiders, while the opposite holds in generic communities [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s22:p0:c3361-5354]. More generally, structuring the multi-community landscape reveals that radically contrasting engagement patterns emerge in different regions of the space, and that these variations can be at least partly explained by the identity type each community fosters [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.09665:s22:p0:c3361-5354].

Moreover, despite rapid progress, deep models remain brittle to subtle distribution shifts, so studying such barely-perceptible perturbations is warranted [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s13:p0:c0-1998].

record.final_answer: The paper argues that the adversarial setting fits misspelling recognition for several reasons: (1) Adversarial misspellings are a real-world phenomenon, not just an academic curiosity — spammers subtly misspell words to evade spam detection while preserving meaning, and communities use similar tricks to evade programmatic Internet censorship [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s13:p0:c1709-3708]. (2) Character-level edits (drops, adds, swaps of internal characters) are psychologically realistic, since humans can still comprehend text whose internal characters are jumbled as long as first and last characters remain intact [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s13:p0:c1709-3708]. (3) Deep models are brittle to such subtle distribution shifts, and an adversary can deliberately degrade a classifier's performance (e.g., a BERT sentiment model dropping from 90.3% to 45.8% accuracy under a single character attack), so robustness to adversarially-chosen misspellings is a meaningful defense target [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s12:p0:c0-980][cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1905.11268:s13:p0:c0-1998].

Since predicting a held-out context word given an input word involves a very large number of possible classes, the task is treated as a ranking problem, and the paper reports the mean reciprocal rank of the correct held-out context words, averaged over 5 train/test splits [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s4:p0:c0-1032]. The paper's models improved MRR by up to 63% over skip-gram on small datasets [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s14:p0:c0-1141].

两篇论文分别回答如下，互不关联：

1. 论文《Mixed Membership Word Embeddings for Computational Social Science》(1705.07368)：MRR 是什么？
MRR 即平均倒数排名（mean reciprocal rank），是一种基于排序的评价指标。由于在给定输入词的情况下预测上下文词涉及大量可能的类别，作者将这一任务视为排序问题，并报告被留出的正确上下文词的平均倒数排名，实验在 5 次训练/测试划分上重复并取平均 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s4:p0:c0-1032]。论文的模型在小数据集上相比 skip-gram 在 MRR 上最多提升 63% [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s14:p0:c0-1141]。

2. 论文《Neural Semantic Parsing in Low-Resource Settings with Back-Translation and Meta-Learning》(1909.05438)：规则是特定于数据集的吗？
不是。论文采用的是简单的、领域无关的映射规则（必要时加上少量领域无关的词级匹配表），而非针对某个数据集的规则，也不依赖标注的逻辑形式或执行结果 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.05438:s0:p1:c0-843]。该规则化设定被应用于三个具有不同领域和程序结构的基准数据集，体现了其通用性 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.05438:s12:p0:c0-1998]。

**问题一：什么是 MRR？**
- 论文一（Mixed Membership Word Embeddings for Computational Social Science）：MRR 即平均倒数排名（mean reciprocal rank）。作者将预测上下文词的任务视为排序问题并报告平均倒数 rank；实验在 5 个训练/测试划分上重复取平均 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s4:p0:c0-1032]。表 4 报告了留出上下文词的 MRR [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s20:p0:c0-1885]，摘要指出小数据集上比 skip-gram 预测性能最高提升 63% MRR [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s14:p0:c0-1141]。
- 论文二（Neural Semantic Parsing in Low-Resource Settings）：可见文本中未使用 MRR；该论文以准确率报告结果（如 WikiSQL 上 72.7%）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.05438:s15:p0:c0-1903]。MRR 是论文一特有的指标概念。

- 论文一：不适用——该论文不涉及“规则”（rules），其核心是混合成员词嵌入模型与主题模型。

**问题一：什么是 MRR？**
- 论文一（Mixed Membership Word Embeddings for Computational Social Science）：MRR 即平均倒数排名（mean reciprocal rank）。作者将预测上下文词的任务视为排序问题并报告平均倒数 rank；实验在 5 个训练/测试划分上重复取平均 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s4:p0:c0-1032]。表 4 报告了留出上下文词的 MRR [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s20:p0:c0-1885]，摘要指出小数据集上比 skip-gram 预测性能最高提升 63% MRR [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1705.07368:s14:p0:c0-1141]。
- 论文二（Neural Semantic Parsing in Low-Resource Settings）：可见文本中未使用 MRR；该论文以准确率报告结果（如 WikiSQL 上 72.7%）[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.05438:s15:p0:c0-1903]。MRR 是论文一特有的指标概念。

**问题二：规则是否是数据集特定的？**
- 论文一：不适用——该论文不涉及“规则”（rules），其核心是混合成员词嵌入模型与主题模型。
- 论文二：不是。论文明确采用简单的、与领域无关的规则（domain-independent rules）来初始化方法，而非标注逻辑形式或答案，并在三个不同领域和程序形式的基准数据集上实验 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.05438:s10:p0:c0-926] [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.05438:s11:p0:c0-1103]。

2. 使用了哪些语言学特征？——该论文并非特征工程式的语义分析工作，未使用语言学特征；其核心组件是数据生成器（语义解析模型+问题生成模型的回译范式）与基于 MAML 的元学习 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1909.05438:s18:p0:c5163-6123]。

**第二篇：Sentiment Analysis for Twitter : Going Beyond Tweet Text (1611.09441)**

1. 规则是否针对特定数据集？——该论文不涉及规则学习/规则覆盖的概念，问题不适用。

2. 使用了哪些语言学特征？——可见摘录确认论文"采用了若干语言学特征以及其他外部信息来源"[cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.09441:s16:p0:c0-658]，且特征超出推文文本本身：包括针对推特媒体特点的特征、来自推文中共享 URL 落地页的外部知识、以及用户/社交媒体特征 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.09441:s15:p0:c0-542]。此外，在预测情感强度时使用了大写词数量、强/弱积极词数量、强/弱消极词数量等特征 [cite:pipaper-full-index-v1-64b1aa77167d5715:1611.09441:s21:p0:c0-1998]。完整的语言特征清单（论文第4节）不在当前可见摘录中，故无法给出完整列表。
